summary: Hermann Hunger is a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster. He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (~1970–1973), University of Chicago (~1973–1978), and University of Vienna (professor, 1978–2007).

Hermann Hupfeld worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1813–1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1817–1819). He later held posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who also worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at Bonn (1875, 1889–1922) and the University of Münster (1876–1885).

Hermann Kopp specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Heidelberg, Leipzig, and the Walleser-Institut under Max Walleser and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at the Pali Text Society, Walleser-Institut, Mainz Academy of Sciences and Literature, and Heidelberg University.

Hermann Kreyenborg was an Indologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Münster, earning his Ph.D. under Richard Schmidt. From 1922 to 1954, he served as a librarian at the University and State Library of Münster.

Hermann Kulke is a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras, Freiburg (under Hermann Goetz and Ulrich Schneider), and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Lommel specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Munich and Göttingen, where Jacob Wackernagel supervised his Ph.D. Lommel held posts at Göttingen (1915, 1917–1920) and Goethe University Frankfurt (1920–1950).

Hermann Mittelberger was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Vienna, the University of Würzburg, Utrecht University, and served as professor of comparative Indo-European at the University of Graz (1971–2003).

Hermann Møller was a linguist who studied at Kiel, Munich, Berlin, Breslau, and Leipzig (under Georg Curtius, earning a Ph.D.). He later served as Privatdozent at Kiel University (1878) and the University of Copenhagen (1883).

Hermann Oesterley worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Music and Theatre Leipzig and earned a Ph.D. at Göttingen. He held posts at Kiel University, Göttingen State and University Library, and Wrocław University Library.

Hermann Oldenberg worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin, completing his doctorate and habilitation under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University (1814) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1816). He held posts at Berlin (~1817–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn (Ph.D. under Hermann Usener), and Leipzig. He held posts as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1875) and professor and director at Heidelberg University (from 1877).

Hermann Paul was a linguist who studied under Heymann Steinthal at Berlin and under Friedrich Zarncke, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien at Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1874, 1877) and the University of Munich (1893–1916).

Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Bernhard Hirzel. He held posts at the University of Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Zürich, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and the University of Göttingen (from 1855).

Hermann Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Munich (-1848) and held a teaching post at Berlin (1851), later becoming a member of the Leopoldina and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Hermann Usener worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn (~1854–1857). He later held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Walter, an Indologist, studied at Edinburgh, Neuchâtel, Tübingen, and Munich, completing a Ph.D. under Ernst Kuhn in 1893. He spent his career at McGill University as a lecturer and professor of modern and Germanic languages (1900–1936).

Hermann Weller was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1897–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1901–1903). He later returned to Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent in 1930 and honorary professor from 1938 to 1952.

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Halle and Berlin, earning his Ph.D. under Franz Bopp. He taught at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule and Gymnasium Schneidemühl before succeeding Bopp as professor of comparative philology at Berlin in 1872.
